cohort: Birthing people experiencing labor with fetal occiput posterior presentation are the focus of this review.
finding: Persistent occiput posterior positions are common malpresentations linked to adverse labor outcomes, and various management strategies, including maternal positioning, instrumental rotation, and manual rotation, have been evaluated with differing levels of evidence regarding their effectiveness and risks.
mod_finding: Persistent OP positions are associated with higher rates of cesarean sections and instrumental deliveries, whereas manual rotation can reduce the operative delivery rate.
